reviews.text: Ukraine 2077

The game doesn't seem to have improved on the "random mission go" system. This means you'll be given incredibly frustrating, nonsensical objectives very early in the game when you're not equipped to deal with them. If you're an average gamer with no FPV experience, you will probably get stuck in the literal 2nd mission. Example: the game starts you with a machine gun that takes 3 shots to kill anything, and a rocket launcher which can't hit moving targets, and which blocks your view with a very over-the-top muzzle flash every time it fires. As early as mission 2, you will have to elliminate flying units, which are tiny on your screen and require pixel-perfect aim. Then, in mission 3, the game assigns you an objective to blow up a bunch of stuff in a confined space, with the same exact weapons, and a shield on top that blocks your shots. Which means you're now having to fly through tiny gaps while shooting at things with ineffective weaponry, where you can fire once every 3-4 seconds because your drone doesn't have enough energy to fire more often. It's just not fun. I can't recommend this game until the mission system is changed to choose objectives appropriately scaled to your current loadout. ------------------------------- On the second attempt, and mission 3 seems to be hardcoded to always be the same "random nonsense go" mission. First it asks you to fly into a cave where you can't hit [i]anything[/i] before first blowing up a shield that blocks all your shots (because that's what "realism" stands for now, I guess). You will lose 80% of your HP here and there is no way around it. Then, it immediately throws 30+ units at you, including: 5 kamikaze drones (ok, pretty realistic and fun), 7 robo mech tanks (what) with laser guns (what), 5 flak cannons, another shield generator, and 8+ automatic minigun turrets. Among all these, there's also 3 random infantry trucks. Yep, 3 regular army trucks. What the ♥♥♥♥ am I playing. I don't know, maybe the game gives you more tactical options later in, that would allow to approach objectives in a different way than "fly at them at max speed and spam guns", but at this point all I have is a minigun and a cluster grenade launcher. It's just not fun and there doesn't appear to be any resemblance of difficulty curve past the 2nd mission. Unlocks also take FOREVER to obtain. The game gives you a laughable amount of upgrade points for completing a misison - about 4000, when a 3rd unlock in line requires... 24.000 or so? Yes, 24 thousands. And that's just the left edge of the tech tree. So you'll be stuck with underpowered weapons all the time. Also why is everything denominated in thousands? It could just be 4 and 24. Overall, at least in early stages, the game plays like a mobile title where the developers overtuned things on purpose to sell you booster packs. Except there's no booster packs. Still, I was lowkey expecting a "Buy 50% damage reduction for $2.99" ad to pop up at the mission debrief screen. The demo was deceptive, too. It devolves into "drones vs aliens" very quickly. This isn't realistic at all.

This has potential, but I can't recommend it right now, especially not at $20. This game may be significantly better on controller, but I got it with the intention of using my radio in order to get some "stick time." There is something off about the physics simulation. I can only describe it as floaty, yet somehow rigid. It's like the drone lacks inertia. The tuning also feels limited and lacks familiarity that a more "Betaflight-esque" rate menu could provide. I can live with this, since it is trying to be both a game, and a sim, but I find that it lacks in both of those departments as a result. Ultrawide support has been improved, but the descriptions of items are poorly organized, difficult to parse, and can even fail to display unless the item is unequipped. Trying to understand dps values beyond vibes is impossible when enemy health and how it scales is never explicitly disclosed. Powerups are also difficult to discern due to their low opacity and the weapons don't really feel that different from one another. The missions feel largely similar as well, with no real difference between enemies or locations. The gameplay also does not meaningfully encourage or promote more aggressive "dodging" playstyles. I find most attacks are either poorly conveyed, or so easily readable that normal flight or low flying is enough to entirely avoid them. The maps also contain environments that range from extremely wide open to claustrophobic, when I feel the sweet spot would be in between, as it would create a space that allows for maneuvering, while still testing your piloting skills. Most fights and flying experiences were not memorable, nor did I feel like it tested or fostered my skills. The exception to this would be the "boss fights." The train in particular was one of my favorite fights, because it enabled me to do matty flips, dolphin dives, and headspins around the train and inside of its tracks. I wish more of the fights were structured similarly, but most were bland gun runs rather than dodging enemy fire with a combination of flips and spins through the environment. I think I mostly want a wider variety of enemies that encourage certain maneuvers to counter them, so I can take advantage of their blindspots, telegraphed attacks, or otherwise. A redesign of the environments would be appreciated as well. I think the newest map (at the time of writing this) is excellent and the way all future maps should head. The piping is fun to fly around and it feels like it was designed to fly around instead of being a set piece. I think this game has potential, but right now, look for other options when it comes to getting stick time.

[h1]This game is AWESOME...even though I kinda SUCK at it![/h1] [h3]One of the coolest concepts applied to a video game I've seen in recent years.[/h3] Who would have thought that making a drone flight simulator combined with combat-shooting gameplay and rogue-lite progression elements would be like capturing lighting in a bottle? This is one of the coolest games I've ever played in the last two decades; such a cool concept that I am surprised it took any developer so long to create such a game until now! Very simple but addicting gameplay loop. You start with nothing unlocked, you complete missions, racking up currency for every enemy you neutralize, and spent your earnings either upgrading your drone's equipment for the current run, or unlocking new content for any future runs. Your drones [b]do NOT[/b] keep all the upgrades you buy for the next time, hence the rogue-lite elements of the game. If you unlock them during gameplay, then you will get to buy said upgrades during your next run, improving your chances of clearing the game. There's a 15 mission strand you are expected to clear all in one go, and you can save your progress and resume your run at any time. Increasing the difficulty level with increase the rewards you earn after clearing a mission. I have only played on Normal so far, which is a good balance for most players; it took me three runs of losing to finally clear the game after having unlocked decent-enough weapons and equipment to survive long enough. There's also other game modes I only tried briefly, like the Survival Mode which is a test of skills to see how long you can last on the battlefield without any pauses or breaks. Like I said in the title of my review, I kinda suck at flying drones, and this game's physics model is remarkably GOOD at demonstrating what it's like to fly a drone. That being said, even if you are new to flying drones or new to any sort of flight simulation game, [b]do yourself a favor and play on Realistic Mode![/b] The Simple Mode's control scheme feels awkward and janky even though the game is doing most of the heavy lifting for controlling the drone. You're going to want full control of the drone yourself; even as an amateur, the Realistic Mode's control scheme is more sensible to understand once you get a feel for the physics. I've been playing this game on an Xbox Series controller and I've been doing just fine. The game's default settings for joystick sensitivity, deadzones and rotational movement are very well-tuned and work very well. [b]If I can do it, then so can you![/b] Half of the dopamine rush that comes from playing this game is flying the drone itself. When you're hurling your drone through obstacles, buildings and tunnels to make those difficult shots on hard-to-reach targets, it's an incredibly satisfying feeling. Can't remember how many times I said "[i]DAMN that was NICE[/i]" when I landed some tricky shots on targets while my drone was at an awkward angle upside-down trying to dodge the kitchen sink of projectiles being thrown at me from every direction. Graphics are acceptable, nothing special but there's a surprising amount of little details here and there. [hr][/hr] [h3]For as much as I enjoyed this game, it still feels like it's in Early Access. Lots of things I'd like to see addressed in the future.[/h3] I played a demo of this game during the Steam Next Fest 2025 event. A lot has changed since this game officially launched, but it needs quite a bit of tweaks from my perspective. [list] [*] The MOST-IMPORTANT thing to me is [b]full controller support, which, as of this review, the game currently lacks.[/b] Most of the UI is able to be navigated by using a controller to move the cursor and select menus and other UI elements, but some of the more-important stuff cannot be selected or configured if you're using only a controller, such as scrolling through the Unlock Tree to browse unlockables, or even selecting a display resolution from the Options menu. There's multiple UI elements that contain multiple tabs or pages which cannot be browsed through with a controller; you have to click through them with your mouse to see the rest of the contents. I'm grateful for the current implementation of controller support, but I'd like to see a complete integration in the near future, hopefully soon. [*] Those [b]Hunter Swarmer drone enemies need to be nerfed![/b] Not only are they fast and unpredictable, but they have too many hit points for a normal enemy encounter and they have incredibly strong, accurate weapons that hit you for big damage. I've lost most of my runs to these guys. They should be tweaked a little bit because they'll prove to be too much for most players, even on Normal difficulty. [/list] [hr][/hr] Other than those things, this game is a blast to play. Glad I discovered it. Here's hoping for continued support from the developers in the future. They've cooked up something great, it would be a shame for it to go to waste!

This game is enjoyable, but it could be so much more. I enjoy flying and shooting stuff, but the missions are really repetitive and there aren't that many types of missions to do. I wish there was an easier way to actually fire the weapons instead of relying on the auto-shooting. I think the 15 level run is a little too long and the difficulty spikes significantly on the last few levels. The music also is not good. There are a lot of unlockable weapons and drones, but it's difficult to compare drones and I wish there was a mode that let you just switch weapons at will so you can play around and see which weapons you actually like. In addition, more mission variations like escorting troops, enemy recon, delivering supplies to your own troops, rescue missions, stealth missions. What this game desperately needs are multiplayer and co-op missions. If that ever releases I'd easily recommend this game.
